events.body:
This is a driver-cancelled trip with a $6.61 no-show fee, so it enters the policy through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver and the driver's stated reason is rider no-show, which routes the case to NS-1/NS-2 [F3][F6][RD-0, NS-0]. Both advocates read the record the same way, and so do I.

NS-1 requires three cumulative conditions. (i) an arrival confirmation exists — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 [F5][NS-1]. claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 599 m at 12:06:55 and he never came within 200 m (F1). The timeline independently confirms the platform never recorded him at the pickup point, driver_arrived_at being null (F4).

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while 600 m from the pickup point, and stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap (F5); his only stationary period, 12:05:55–12:09:25, was spent 600 m away (F2). NS-1 (ii) and (iii) therefore both fail.

The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" (F12) is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records in F1, F2, F4 and F5, and the system records win; the statement cannot satisfy NS-1.

The rider was at the pickup point throughout and said so while the driver was still stationary elsewhere: chat #2 at 12:07, "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" (F9), a message the driver never answered before cancelling at 12:09:25 (F3).

The driver's own chat shows the arrival claim was internal to his stationary position away from the pickup: chat #1 at 12:06, "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out" (F8), followed by chat #3 at 12:09, "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" (F10).

No external cause explains the driver's position: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window (F14), only a moderate band-3 flow on Jalan Besar (F13), and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F15).
The $6.61 cancellation fee charged (F6, F3) is not supported by any NS-1 condition, so the full amount falls to be refunded under NS-2; no surge applied (F7).

Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while his GPS placed him 600 m from the pickup point (F5), the case additionally warrants flag_account as abuse of the arrival/cancellation button, supported by his 90-day record of 1 dispute, 1 upheld on a no-show (F17).
The chat record is complete — 3 messages, every one timestamped (F11) — so the no-show determination can be made on this record and no G12 incompleteness escalation is required.

weaknesses: The chat record is short (F11) and the driver did message the rider at 12:06 saying he was "here already" (F8); the other side will argue the rider should have searched harder or boarded, but F1/F2/F5 place the car 600 m away, so the message cannot be read as arrival at the pickup.

The rider profile is thin (F16: rating 4.4, no dispute history) and there is no rider-side GPS fact placing the rider at the pickup point — the rider's presence rests on chat #2 (F9), which the other side may argue is an uncorroborated statement, though the system's own GPS record (F1, F5, F4) is what defeats the driver's arrival claim.

The rider's claim that they "waited the whole time" is supported only by F9 and the absence of any contrary record; if the judge wants claimant-side GPS it is not in the fact table, though NS-2 does not require the rider to prove presence — it requires the driver to prove the NS-1 conditions.

claims.assertion: The complaint's central factual premise is confirmed by the record: the driver never reached the pickup point — closest approach 599 m at 12:06:55, and the platform never recorded an arrival (driver_arrived_at is null), so on the GPS record there was no valid 'at the pick-up location' arrival.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while 600 m from the pickup point, far outside the 200 m arrival radius, and stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap; requirement NS-1(i)/(ii) therefore fails on the record.

Even if the tap counted as arrival, the driver was stationary 12:05:55–12:09:25 at a point 600 m from the pickup and never inside 200 m at any time, so the NS-1(iii) condition of continuously waiting at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes is not met.

The driver's written statement that he waited at the pickup and cancelled a genuine no-show (F12) is contradicted by the system records F1, F2, F4 and F5, so it cannot carry the case; the cancellation was made at 12:09:25 without the arrival conditions ever being satisfied.

The rider's account is consistent with the records rather than with a bare denial: she wrote at 12:07 that she was at the pickup point and saw no car (F9), which matches GPS showing no vehicle within 200 m (F1, F2).

The rider's message is not merely non-response: chat #2 at 12:07 asked where the driver was while the driver sat 600 m away, and the driver's reply at 12:09 asserting 'more than 3 min already' was measured from a tap made outside the arrival radius, not from a compliant wait.

No external cause excuses the failure to reach the pickup point: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so the 599 m stand-off was not forced by road or weather conditions.

Because the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F6) rests on a no-show claim that fails NS-1(i)–(iii), the rider should not bear it; the fee was charged without a valid arrival, and the fare facts show no surge or other published add-on that could independently justify it.

The account-history facts are relevant only to what action follows, not to whether the no-show fee stands: the driver has 2295 days of tenure, a 4.67 rating and 464 trips in 90 days, but also 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F17).

Tapping "I'm Here" 600 m from the pickup point and then cancelling on that basis falls within the platform's abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-button conduct that NS-2 attaches a flag_account consequence to; this is an account-review consequence of the failed arrival conditions, not an independent finding.

weaknesses: The strongest point against my client is F1 and F5 together: the closest approach was 599 m and the "I'm Here" tap was made 600 m out with 0 s spent inside 200 m afterwards — this is the rider's best evidence and it is a system record that my own side cannot rebut.

My client's written statement (F12) claims he waited at the pickup and the rider never showed up; the record shows the opposite (F2, F4, F5), so the other side will use F12 as an inconsistency to attack his credibility throughout.

The GPS shows my client stationary 3 min 30 s (F2), which the rider may well reframe as a genuine wait (F2, F5) and argue he was trying in good faith, which cuts against any suggestion of intentional abuse and weakens the flag_account limb.

The driver's profile shows 1 no-show dispute upheld in 90 days (F17), which the rider will rely on under the NS-2 account-flag limb, while F16 shows the rider has a clean 90-day record and a 4.4 rating, so the judge has no basis to doubt her account of waiting.

The single cancelled trip also implicates cancellation-rate consequences under NS-3, and the traffic band evidence (F13, band 3 = 20–29 km/h on Jalan Besar) could be spun by the other side as mild congestion, though F14 (no incidents) leaves it as weak support for any congestion excuse.

points.response: Accepted — this is my own case and nothing in it needs contesting: F1 and F4 show the driver never came within 200 m and the platform recorded no arrival, so NS-1 (ii) fails.
Accepted: F5 places the "I'm Here" tap at 600 m with 0 s inside 200 m afterwards, so NS-1 (i)/(ii) fail and the fee must be refunded under NS-2.
Accepted: F2 shows the only stationary period, 12:05:55–12:09:25, was spent 600 m from the pickup with no time inside 200 m, so NS-1 (iii) is not met.
Accepted: F12 is contradicted by the system records F1, F2, F4 and F5 and cannot carry the no-show claim.
Accepted, and it reinforces C4: F9 (rider at the pickup, no car) matches F1 and F2, which put the car 600 m away.
Accepted: the 12:09 "more than 3 min already" message (F10) was timed from a tap made 600 m out (F5), not from a compliant wait at the pickup.

Accepted: F14 and F15 show no incident and fair weather, so nothing external forced the 599 m stand-off in F1; the moderate band-3 flow on Jalan Besar (F13) explains neither a 600 m distance nor the failure to arrive.
Accepted: with NS-1 (i)–(iii) all failing, F6's $6.61 fee rests on nothing and is refundable in full under NS-2; no surge or published add-on (F7) saves it.
Accepted as to relevance only: F17 (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) goes to the account flag, not to the finding, which already stands on F1, F2, F4 and F5 under NS-2.

Accepted as to the account limb: F5 and F2 (tap 600 m out, stationary 600 m away, 0 s inside 200 m) fall within the button abuse NS-2 attaches flag_account to, and F17 shows the rider's 90-day record is clean (F16) while the driver already has one upheld no-show dispute.
Conceded — the GPS record (F1, closest approach 599 m at 12:06:55; F4, driver_arrived_at null) defeats any arrival claim on the NS-1 (ii) limb, and my own case already rests on that record.
Conceded as to the conditions: the tap at 12:06:15 was made 600 m out with 0 s inside 200 m afterwards (F5) and the only stationary period (F2) was spent 600 m away, so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail.
Conceded — my client's post-hoc statement (F12) cannot stand against the system records F1, F2, F4 and F5; I do not put it forward as proof of a valid arrival.

Conceded on the substance: the rider's 12:07 message (F9) matches the GPS showing no vehicle within 200 m (F1, F2), and the driver cancelled at 12:09:25 (F3) after the valid arrival conditions had already failed. I note only that F9 is a statement, and it is the system records F1/F2/F5 — not F9 — that decide the arrival question.

Partly conceded: chat #3 asserting 'more than 3 min already' (F10) measures time from a tap made outside the 200 m radius (F5), so it does not evidence a compliant wait; my client's own 12:06 message (F8) is contradicted by F1/F2/F5. But F8 shows he announced a silver Toyota Altis, which the rider could have located nearby — a point that goes to rider credulity, not to NS-1 compliance.

The absence of incidents (F14) and fair weather (F15) are accepted: nothing external forced the 599 m stand-off (F1). Band-3 flow at 20–29 km/h on Jalan Besar (F13) is normal flow, not severe congestion, and I do not rely on it as an excuse.

Agreed that the $6.61 on record (F6, F3) is not supported by NS-1 as charged, and no surge applied (F7); the fee should be refunded to the rider under NS-2. My only reservation is that NS-2 also attaches flag_account for a tap made outside the arrival radius, so the account consequence is a matter for review rather than a finding I can contest.

Conceded that the tap at 600 m (F5, F2) engages NS-2's flag_account limb and that my client's profile records 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F17); I ask the judge to weigh the 6.3-year tenure, 4.67 rating and 464 trips in 90 days (F17) as mitigation rather than an aggravating pattern.
Accepted: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F11), so no G12 incompleteness escalation is needed and the fee question can be decided on the record.
Withdrawn: my attempt to frame the profile facts as neutral to the finding is overtaken by the system records F1, F2, F4 and F5, so D9 and D10 standing on F17 alone should not affect the outcome.
